original_question: Classify all K-derivations delta of general type on the polynomial ring R = K[x, y], where "general type" means that A_0 = {x in R : delta(x) = 0} and L_0 = {xi in Q(R) : delta(xi) = 0} both equal K, and describe such derivations in terms of the delta-integral ring A generated by delta-integral elements.
target_in_paper: The draft is aiming at Conjecture 1.1 in the paper’s derivation/Darboux-polynomial subsection: for a K-derivation δ of R = K[x,y] of general type (i.e. A_0 = Ker(δ|_R) = K and L_0 = Ker(δ|_{Q(R)}) = K), determine the structure of the K-subalgebra A generated by the δ-integral elements. The paper’s target is not a broad classification of all such derivations up to change of coordinates, but the sharp structural question about whether the δ-integral ring is generated by one polynomial.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ambient ring R = K[x,y], the derivation δ, the two constant fields/rings A_0 and L_0 used to define 'general type', and the fact that the paper formulates the problem in terms of the δ-integral ring A generated by δ-integral elements.
missing_details: The paper’s question is narrower than 'classify all derivations': it asks for the structure of the δ-integral ring A for derivations of general type, not a full automorphism-by-automorphism classification of δ.
The base-field assumptions need to be stated exactly as in the paper (in this context, the nearby discussion should be checked for whether K is assumed algebraically closed and of characteristic 0).
You need to define Q(R) explicitly as the fraction field of R.
You need to define 'δ-integral element' explicitly, rather than only referring to the ring A generated by them.
The quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether every derivation δ of general type on K[x,y] has the stated property for A.
The stand-alone question should say whether the trivial case A = K is allowed, or whether the intended conclusion is A = K[p] for some single nonconstant/irreducible polynomial p.
If the nearby propositions/theorem specify irreducibility, closedness, or uniqueness-up-to-scalar of the generator p, that should be included.

The draft omits the fact that Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 are used in the paper to sharpen the formulation, so the final question should be phrased in the same 'ring A of δ-integral elements' language rather than as an unrestricted classification problem.
refined_question: Let K be as in the paper, let R = K[x,y], let Q(R) be its fraction field, and let δ be a nonzero K-derivation of R. Set A_0 = {f in R : δ(f)=0} and L_0 = {ξ in Q(R) : δ(ξ)=0}, and assume that δ is of general type, i.e. A_0 = L_0 = K. For a nonzero f in R, call f δ-integral if δ(f) is divisible by f in R (equivalently, δ(f)=bf for some b in R), and let A be the K-subalgebra of R generated by all δ-integral elements. Is it true that, for every derivation δ of general type on K[x,y], the δ-integral ring A is generated by a single polynomial (equivalently, apart from the trivial case A=K, one has A=K[p] for some single nonconstant δ-integral polynomial p)?
justification: The paper-faithful target is the structural conjecture stated as Conjecture 1.1, with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 supplying the precise surrounding notation and reformulation in terms of the δ-integral ring A. Your draft is close in spirit, but it is broader than the paper because it asks for a complete classification of all general-type derivations. The paper’s actual intent is the sharper question: for derivations of general type on K[x,y], how restrictive is the collection of δ-integral elements, and in particular is the K-algebra they generate forced to be singly generated? That is the narrow, stand-alone form that stays closest to the paper’s own formulation.
